subject: Workplace Skills
title: Self-Determination Theory
description: A quick, practical guide to Self-Determination Theory.

hook.text: Deci and Ryan spent 40 years proving that humans need autonomy, competence, and relatedness to thrive.

buildup.text: When any of these three needs is blocked, motivation withers. People disengage even if the salary is high.

discovery.text: Autonomy means choice in how you work. Competence means progress. Relatedness means genuine connection.

twist.text: Micromanagement attacks all three at once. It removes choice, signals distrust, and isolates the individual.

climax.text: Check which of the three is missing when team morale drops. Usually one specific need is being starved.

punchline.text: Autonomy, competence, connection. Feed all three.

quiz.question: Why does micromanagement destroy motivation according to SDT?
options: It wastes the manager's time on trivial oversight
It attacks autonomy, signals distrust, and isolates people
It only affects junior employees who lack confidence
